- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk reversal or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — if last 3–5 prices show a sharp rise, cap forecast increase to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — if true outcome shows strong upward trend after day 15–20, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for remaining days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — use sentiment-weighted smoothing to align with sentiment direction.
